title: Benchmark v3 verdict: LEAN consult = cost PARITY (1.03×) vs fat consult's 1.63× — payload size WAS the overhead
summary: v3 (graph-dependent, opus, n=5, all 10 solved, 0 contamination) tested ON arm with --consult=lean (get_learnings compact:true, ~1-3k payload) vs OFF. RESULT — cost-weighted gross ON/OFF = 1.025× (ON 142,278 ± 18,818 vs OFF 138,817 ± 12,119 tok-eq) = PARITY, within overlapping variance/noise. Raw gross ON/OFF = 1.151×. Cost NET ON/OFF = 0.352× (the agent WITH context did ~65% less non-orchestrator work). THE ARC: v1 (orchestrator unused) = neutral; v2 (forced FAT consult, ~25k payload) = +63% cost overhead (cost gross 1.63×); v3 (forced LEAN consult, ~1-3k compact payload) = +2.5% = parity. CONCLUSION: the v2 "+63% overhead" was almost entirely PAYLOAD SIZE (dumping the whole verdicts/failures/recent store, re-attended every turn as cache_read). The lazy-context fix (compact get_learnings) removes essentially the entire gap → consulting the orchestrator graph is now cost-NEUTRAL. The agent still does far less actual work with context (net 0.35×); lean consult means that work-saving is no longer erased by the consult overhead. HONEST BOUNDS: it's PARITY not an outright cost-WIN (gross is a wash; the consult still costs ~what it saves on this self-solvable task); n=5 ~13% variance so 1.03× ≡ 1.0; both arms solved 5/5 (no quality delta on this task — it was solvable either way); cost weights approximate; schema tax under-counted. The real upside (memory, coordination, rework-avoidance, parallelism) sits ON TOP of now-free context delivery — not measured by this single-task token bench. Validates the lazy-router architecture (compact + pointers + weighted scoped traversal): make the payload lean and context delivery stops costing anything.
